applied_items.content:
Canonical ownership of declared paths SHALL be resolved when the definition is
approved, and a change that has never closed SHALL be able to correct an
acceptance input owner without an audited reopen event.

Acceptance Criteria

- Approving a definition rejects declared paths that no declared module
  canonically owns, naming every offending path in one error.
- Paths that do not yet exist are not rejected at approve, since the owning spec
  may claim them in the same change; they remain enforced at finalize.
- A declared path that is a directory is not file-level ownership-checked at
  approve; its descendant files remain checked at finalize.
- Recognized reserved delivery paths (for example files under `.github/` or
  `docs/`, and the protected SDD and root metadata files) are signed with the
  exact delivery owner by design and finalize accepts them, so they are not
  ownership refusals at approve and not `correct-owner` discovery candidates.
- A change with justified `no_spec_change` and no declared specs is
  ownership-checked at approve as well: an existing production-source path in
  its scope that is not recognized reserved delivery metadata has no declared
  owner, so it is rejected, naming the module that owns it, before anyone
  approves or reviews it (#986, #956). Empty specs without that justification
  still fail closed at definition validation and at ownership validation.
- A change at verifying that has never closed may correct an acceptance input
  owner under a currently valid definition approval. That substitute is for
  guided-path reachability, not audit-equivalent provenance to an
  Accepted→reopen cycle.
- A change that did close continues to require an audited reopen, unchanged.
- Owner recovery never prints a command that cannot run as printed: when a
  module name cannot round-trip through the comma-separated `affected_specs`
  answer, the guidance names the modules in prose instead. When the spec
  listing exceeds its bound, the recovery says the listing is incomplete rather
  than omitting an owner. A recovery that replaces `affected_specs` says the
  constraints answer must be renewed before approval. Owner discovery includes
  registry-registered canonical specs outside the specs directory.
- The ship preflight and review owner recovery declares owners only for unowned
  inputs the change modified (since its base commit or the merge base with the
  remote default branch, or untracked); an unowned input it never modified is named
  with a recovery that narrows `affected_paths` instead, since its owner has nothing
  to approve in this change (#1000). Approve's own ownership refusal is unchanged.
  Without a usable base commit, a merge base with the remote default branch, or a
  complete spec listing, every input keeps the declare recovery, and a base commit
  that is not a full commit id is never passed to Git.

applied_items.content:
`specsync change ship [ID]` SHALL run ship preflight for one change and, when
`ready_to_finalize` is true, perform finalize. When not ready it SHALL exit
non-zero and print blockers and the next stage without mutating state.
Ship preflight, including `--dry-run`, SHALL run the canonical-ownership check
finalize runs over the change's delivery inputs. A production-source input that
no declared module owns SHALL be a blocker naming the path, the module that owns
it, and the recovery (`specsync change send-back <id>`, then
`specsync change answer <id> affected_specs <modules>`); `change ship-status`
SHALL report the same blocker and SHALL NOT report the change ready to finalize
(#986, #956). An unowned input the change has not modified since its base
commit SHALL instead be named with a narrowing recovery
(`specsync change send-back <id>`, then
`specsync change answer <id> affected_paths '<path>,<path>'` naming only what the
change edits), because declaring its owner would pull an untouched module into the
change (#1000). An input counts as modified when it differs from the base commit
or from the merge base with the remote default branch, or is untracked; without a usable base commit, a merge base with the remote default branch, or a
complete spec listing, every input keeps the declare recovery. When both kinds are
present, one send-back carries both answers. An untouched input whose owners the
declare answer already declares is not narrowed.

Optional orchestration flags after a successful finalize (or for already-archived
changes):

- `--push` SHALL commit the archive tip when the working tree is dirty and run
  `git push` for the current branch.
- `--wait` SHALL poll GitHub check-runs for HEAD (using the same in-process REST
  path as ship-status trust) until overall status is `green`, `failed`, timeout,
  or offline/`GITHUB_TOKEN` absent (reported as `local_guidance` without failing
  when no token).
- `--wait-timeout-secs` SHALL bound the wait (default 900).
- `--dry-run` SHALL refuse combination with `--push` or `--wait`.

Acceptance Criteria

- Exit code 0 only when preflight is clean and finalize succeeds (or the change
  is already archived and nothing remains), and optional push/wait succeed.
- Exit code non-zero when blockers remain, push fails, wait sees failed checks,
  or wait times out.
- Text and JSON outputs name the current tip class and next ship stage; JSON may
  include `push` and `wait` result objects when those flags are used.
- When sibling active changes remain after finalize, next guidance names them and
  requires their own check → review → ship cycle before merge.
- A no-spec-change change whose directory scope delivers production source a
  module owns is not ready: `change ship-status` names the blocker and the
  recovery, `change ship --dry-run` exits non-zero, and running the named
  recovery ships it (#986, #956).
- When a directory scope covers an unowned file the change never modified, the
  recovery names that file and says to narrow `affected_paths`; a modified
  unowned file in the same scope keeps the declare-the-owner recovery (#1000).
